symptom: A fall-through custom error handler (no return / raise error) on an activity inside an IF, CASE or split type branch was wired outside the branch. With a result variable it rejoined on the flow INTO the split, so a failing call re-ran the decision and called again (a loop; DESCRIBE shows `merge rejoin1;` before the `if`). Without one it ended the microflow at an end event of its own (DESCRIBE shows a `return;` the script did not contain). In a branch ending in return it rejoined after the IF. `mx check` reports 0 errors for all of them (mendixlabs/mxcli#1565).
cause: The builder keeps the handler pending until the next flow is drawn from the failing activity. buildFlowGraph settles it on every flow it draws, but the branch loops settled only an EMPTY handler (`if fb.emptyErrorHandlerFrom == lastID`), and the IF-without-ELSE and split type loops not even that, so a handler with a body left the branch pending. The parent draws the flow into the split only after building it, and a handler with a result variable settles on the next flow whatever its origin: that flow was the one into the split. Without a result variable nothing matched, and the end-of-flow pass gave it an end event.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_flows.go (enterBranchErrorHandlers / takeBranchErrorHandlers / settleBranchErrorHandlersOn / addBranchErrorHandlerFlowForStatement / queueBranchErrorHandlersAt; addPendingErrorHandlerFlowTo removed), cmd_microflows_builder_control.go (IF: all three branch loops settle on each flow and on the exit flow to the merge; leftovers rejoin on the flow leaving the IF; thenNeedsErrorMerge removed), cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go (CASE and split type branches); test cmd_microflows_builder_branch_handler_test.go; example mdl-examples/bug-tests/1565-branch-error-handler-rejoin.mdl
insight: Making the branch loops settle on every flow is not enough on its own. (1) The handlers pending when a split starts belong to the activity BEFORE it, and a result-variable handler settles on any flow, so it would rejoin in the middle of the first branch: each branch sets the outer handlers aside and restores them. (2) In a branch that ends in return, a result-variable handler is deliberately sent to the code after the split, the shared error path of a success tail built on the result (TestBuildFlowGraph_OutputHandlerInReturningBranchSkipsDerivedSuccessTail); left pending, it would settle on the next flow the parent draws, the one INTO the split. Such leftovers are pinned to the split exit (merge, continuing branch, or the split itself when every branch returns) by making that exit their source and clearing the skip variable, so they settle on the flow leaving the split. Assert the graph (where the handler tail reaches through merges, end-event count, no cycle), not mx check, which accepts every broken shape.
